# Harness support matrix

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/harness-matrix.ts from the adapter registry. Do not hand-edit: change the adapter declaration and re-run the script. -->

Spec §4.7: this page is the FIRST of the three capability inputs — what the adapter declares as implemented. It is never a session's capability on its own: whether this machine can provide it (inventory + admission) and what this session can do now (the selected driver's live handle) are answered separately. The served descriptor derives its "implemented" flags from the same registry rows this page renders (`sectionStatusesOf` in `packages/harness/src/registry.ts`).

The `descriptor` and `catalog` Adapter sections (spec §4.1/§4.5) are NOT rows above: they are plain required `AgentManifest` fields — never `Declared`, never declined, so there is nothing to walk — and their totality is a typecheck, not a cell. A harness without presentation cannot be offered.

## claude-code — supported 26/30

- `runtime.server`: Claude Code ships no server mode — the Agent SDK is in-process and `claude -p` is one-shot
- `runtime.context.codex-app-server`: This Claude driver has no verified native context observation mechanism
- `runtime.context.opencode-server`: This Claude driver has no verified native context observation mechanism
- `runtime.context.opencode2-server`: This Claude driver has no verified native context observation mechanism
- `runtime.context.grok-acp`: This Claude driver has no verified native context observation mechanism
- `runtime.context.fake`: This Claude driver has no verified native context observation mechanism
- `usage.history`: Claude Code writes no recoverable quota history — its usage endpoint is read live and cached nowhere, by Podium or by Claude Code
- `headless.buildExec`: the Claude Agent SDK builds its own invocation in-process
- `transcript.sqliteLocator`: this harness stores transcripts in files — there is no database to locate

## codex — supported 26/32

- `inventory.loginCommandProbe`: Codex login detection still uses its guarded local auth file
- `runtime.embedded`: Codex ships a server, not a library to host in-process
- `runtime.context.opencode-server`: This Codex driver has no verified context telemetry source
- `runtime.context.opencode2-server`: This Codex driver has no verified context telemetry source
- `runtime.context.grok-acp`: This Codex driver has no verified context telemetry source
- `runtime.context.claude-sdk`: This Codex driver has no verified context telemetry source
- `runtime.context.fake`: This Codex driver has no verified context telemetry source
- `usage.history`: Recovered Codex windows disagree with live sampling (used_percent resets inside a window while resets_at moves backwards); Codex history is left to live sampling
- `transcript.recordColor`: this harness does not report an identity colour in its records
- `transcript.sqliteLocator`: this harness stores transcripts in files — there is no database to locate
- `credentials.transfer`: Codex credentials live in a plain file; no platform transfer applies

## grok — supported 23/32

- `composer`: grok has no composer scrape rules yet
- `handoffTranscript`: cross-machine handoff is not supported for grok sessions
- `conversationFile`: grok declares no conversation file to move between its homes
- `classifyBrowserOpen`: no catalogued grok login/link domains yet — the daemon generic redirect_uri heuristic decides (POD-738)
- `inventory.loginCommandProbe`: Grok login detection still uses its local credential file
- `runtime.embedded`: grok ships no library to host in-process
- `runtime.context.codex-app-server`: This Grok driver has no verified context observation mechanism
- `runtime.context.opencode-server`: This Grok driver has no verified context observation mechanism
- `runtime.context.opencode2-server`: This Grok driver has no verified context observation mechanism
- `runtime.context.claude-sdk`: This Grok driver has no verified context observation mechanism
- `runtime.context.generic-pty`: Grok terminal status requires shared config.toml; measured launch overlays ignore ui.status_line, so no isolated status bridge is available. Persisted signals lag inference
- `runtime.context.fake`: This Grok driver has no verified context observation mechanism
- `runtime.context.headless`: Grok --single has no verified fresh context channel; persisted signals lag inference and usage ledgers are turn accounting
- `transcript.recordColor`: this harness does not report an identity colour in its records
- `transcript.sqliteLocator`: this harness stores transcripts in files — there is no database to locate
- `credentials.transfer`: Grok credentials live in a plain file; no platform transfer applies

## opencode — supported 12/28

- `credentials`: OpenCode credential portability is not supported yet
- `usage`: OpenCode exposes no vendor quota endpoint and stores transcripts in SQLite — no harvest layout to declare yet
- `install`: OpenCode is distributed through npm, brew, and its own standalone installer — no single vendor install script to run
- `instrumentation`: opencode posts no hook payloads; observation is poll-only over its event stream and store
- `composer`: opencode has no composer scrape rules; sessions drive through its server protocol
- `handoffTranscript`: cross-machine handoff is not supported for opencode sessions
- `conversationFile`: opencode declares no conversation file to move between its homes
- `classifyBrowserOpen`: no catalogued opencode login/link domains yet — the daemon generic redirect_uri heuristic decides (POD-738)
- `inventory.loginCommandProbe`: OpenCode login detection still uses its local authentication database
- `inventory.loginIdentity`: OpenCode does not expose a stable local account identity yet
- `inventory.portableCredential`: OpenCode credential portability is not supported yet
- `runtime.embedded`: opencode ships a server, not a library to host in-process
- `runtime.context.codex-app-server`: OpenCode context observation is unavailable for this driver
- `runtime.context.grok-acp`: OpenCode context observation is unavailable for this driver
- `runtime.context.claude-sdk`: OpenCode context observation is unavailable for this driver
- `runtime.context.fake`: OpenCode context observation is unavailable for this driver
- `runtime.context.headless`: OpenCode headless context has no verified invocation-owned native source
- `transcript.recordToItems`: opencode maps typed SQLite rows rather than native JSONL records
- `transcript.recordRuntime`: opencode reports no model, effort or context use in its records
- `transcript.recordColor`: opencode has no identity-colour record
- `transcript.chainPaths`: opencode stores transcripts in SQLite — there are no files to chain

## cursor — supported 9/26

- `credentials`: Cursor credential portability is not supported yet
- `usage`: Cursor exposes no declared quota endpoint or transcript harvest layout yet
- `install`: cursor-agent is distributed through Cursor's own installer (curl https://cursor.com/install | bash)
- `instrumentation`: Cursor posts no hook payloads; observation is poll-only over its transcript
- `composer`: Cursor has no composer scrape rules yet
- `handoffTranscript`: cross-machine handoff is not supported for cursor sessions
- `conversationFile`: cursor declares no conversation file to move between its homes
- `classifyBrowserOpen`: no catalogued cursor login/link domains yet — the daemon generic redirect_uri heuristic decides (POD-738)
- `inventory.loginCommand`: Cursor does not expose a supported native login command yet
- `inventory.loginCommandProbe`: Cursor has no supported native login-status command
- `inventory.loginIdentity`: Cursor does not expose a stable local account identity yet
- `inventory.portableCredential`: Cursor credential portability is not supported yet
- `runtime.server`: no verified server mode: the public ACP registry lists Cursor as an agent, but nobody has probed cursor-agent the way POD-2025 probed grok — verify before turning this into a spec
- `runtime.embedded`: cursor-agent ships no library to host in-process
- `runtime.context.codex-app-server`: No Cursor context implementation is declared for this driver
- `runtime.context.opencode-server`: No Cursor context implementation is declared for this driver
- `runtime.context.opencode2-server`: No Cursor context implementation is declared for this driver
- `runtime.context.grok-acp`: No Cursor context implementation is declared for this driver
- `runtime.context.claude-sdk`: No Cursor context implementation is declared for this driver
- `runtime.context.generic-pty`: Cursor terminal transcripts expose no validated current-context usage or effective capacity; Auto/provider capacity is unknown
- `runtime.context.fake`: No Cursor context implementation is declared for this driver
- `runtime.context.headless`: Cursor headless text and documented JSON/stream-JSON results expose no validated current-context usage or effective capacity; a model display name does not establish Auto/provider capacity
- `transcript.recordRuntime`: this harness does not report model, effort or context use in its records
- `transcript.recordColor`: this harness does not report an identity colour in its records
- `transcript.sqliteLocator`: this harness stores transcripts in files — there is no database to locate

## pi — supported 13/27

- `usage`: Pi exposes no declared quota endpoint or transcript harvest layout yet
- `install`: Pi is distributed through npm, its standalone installer, and GitHub releases — no single vendor install script to run
- `composer`: pi has no composer scrape rules yet
- `handoffTranscript`: cross-machine handoff is not supported for pi sessions
- `classifyBrowserOpen`: no catalogued pi login/link domains yet — the daemon generic redirect_uri heuristic decides
- `inventory.loginCommand`: Pi signs in through its interactive /login command
- `inventory.loginCommandProbe`: Pi login detection reads its local auth.json
- `inventory.portableCredential`: Pi logins are never copied between machines
- `runtime.server`: pi --mode rpc is a real JSONL-over-stdio server mode, but Podium has not driven it yet — verify before turning it into a spec
- `runtime.embedded`: pi ships an SDK, but it is not hosted in-process yet
- `runtime.context.codex-app-server`: Pi has no admitted context mechanism on this driver; RPC/server remains unimplemented
- `runtime.context.opencode-server`: Pi has no admitted context mechanism on this driver; RPC/server remains unimplemented
- `runtime.context.opencode2-server`: Pi has no admitted context mechanism on this driver; RPC/server remains unimplemented
- `runtime.context.grok-acp`: Pi has no admitted context mechanism on this driver; RPC/server remains unimplemented
- `runtime.context.claude-sdk`: Pi has no admitted context mechanism on this driver; RPC/server remains unimplemented
- `runtime.context.fake`: Pi has no admitted context mechanism on this driver; RPC/server remains unimplemented
- `transcript.recordColor`: this harness does not report an identity colour in its records
- `transcript.sqliteLocator`: this harness stores transcripts in files — there is no database to locate
- `credentials.transfer`: Pi credentials live in a plain file; no platform transfer applies

## antigravity — supported 18/30

- `managedInstall`: Antigravity releases and updater not yet measured for a Podium-managed install
- `composer`: Antigravity composer rendering varies by terminal; submit receipt verification uses native transcript echoes
- `handoffTranscript`: The native conversation SQLite/protobuf stores have no verified portable export contract
- `conversationFile`: antigravity declares no conversation file to move between its homes
- `inventory.loginCommandProbe`: Antigravity has no non-interactive login-status command; readiness reads its native token store
- `inventory.portableCredential`: Google logins are signed into isolated homes on each machine; shared OS-keyring credentials are never automatically propagated
- `runtime.server`: agy acp is available upstream; Podium currently drives Antigravity headless sessions with the verified structured print protocol
- `runtime.embedded`: Antigravity is a native executable; Podium does not embed its Python SDK
- `usage.history`: Antigravity does not persist quota-window samples in its conversation logs
- `transcript.recordColor`: this harness does not report an identity colour in its records
- `transcript.sqliteLocator`: this harness stores transcripts in files — there is no database to locate
- `credentials.transfer`: Google subscription homes use native remote sign-in; automatic copying of OS-keyring credentials is not supported

## Default posture by launch mode

What `{"mode":"autonomous"}` comes to for a current install, from each adapter's posture section (`packages/harness/src/adapters/<harness>/posture.ts`). `met`: by a flag, inline config or by default. `home edit`: only by an edit to the harness home. `unmet`: this launch cannot meet it; the reasons follow the table. The mode column is the harness mode Podium asks for.

| harness | launch | mode | workspace-trust | podium-cli | autonomy | quiet-start | podium-material |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| claude-code | terminal | `auto` | home edit | met | met | met | met |
| claude-code | engine | `auto` | home edit | met | met | met | met |
| claude-code | turn | `auto` | home edit | met | met | met | met |
| claude-code | client | `auto` | home edit | met | met | met | met |
| codex | terminal | `auto-review` | met | home edit | met | unmet | met |
| codex | engine | `auto-review` | met | home edit | met | met | met |
| codex | turn | `auto-review` | met | home edit | met | met | met |
| codex | client | none | met | home edit | met | unmet | met |
| grok | terminal | `auto` | unmet | met | met | met | met |
| grok | engine | `auto` | met | home edit | met | met | met |
| grok | turn | `auto` | unmet | met | met | met | met |
| grok | client | `auto` | unmet | met | met | met | met |
| opencode | terminal | `auto` | met | met | met | met | met |
| opencode | engine | none | met | met | met | met | met |
| opencode | turn | `auto` | met | met | met | met | met |
| opencode | client | none | met | met | met | met | met |
| cursor | terminal | none | unmet | unmet | unmet | unmet | unmet |
| cursor | engine | `auto-review` | met | unmet | met | met | unmet |
| cursor | turn | `auto-review` | met | unmet | met | met | unmet |
| cursor | client | none | unmet | unmet | unmet | unmet | unmet |
| pi | terminal | none | met | met | met | met | met |
| pi | engine | none | met | met | met | met | met |
| pi | turn | none | met | met | met | met | met |
| pi | client | none | met | met | met | met | met |
| antigravity | terminal | `auto` | unmet | met | met | met | met |
| antigravity | engine | `auto` | met | met | met | met | met |
| antigravity | turn | `auto` | met | met | unmet | met | met |
| antigravity | client | `auto` | unmet | met | met | met | met |

Unmet, and why:

- codex, terminal, `quiet-start`: Codex of unknown version is not measured to take trust for Podium's hooks per launch (from 0.147.0), so it may ask to review them at startup
- codex, client, `quiet-start`: Codex of unknown version is not measured to take trust for Podium's hooks per launch (from 0.147.0), so it may ask to review them at startup
- grok, terminal, `workspace-trust`: Grok of unknown version is not known to take --trust (from 1.0.5), so it may ask whether to trust the folder
- grok, turn, `workspace-trust`: Grok of unknown version is not known to take --trust (from 1.0.5), so it may ask whether to trust the folder
- grok, client, `workspace-trust`: Grok of unknown version is not known to take --trust (from 1.0.5), so it may ask whether to trust the folder
- cursor, terminal, `workspace-trust`: Cursor keeps interactive folder trust in private state that Podium does not write
- cursor, terminal, `podium-cli`: Cursor takes allow rules only from a settings file shared with every Cursor session, which Podium does not edit
- cursor, terminal, `autonomy`: unmeasured: Cursor's mode flags were not run in its terminal UI (no signed-in Cursor account was available to the spike), so it starts in the mode its own settings choose
- cursor, terminal, `quiet-start`: unmeasured: no signed-in Cursor account was available to the spike
- cursor, terminal, `podium-material`: unmeasured: whether Cursor asks before reading Podium's attachments outside the working folder; no signed-in Cursor account was available to the spike
- cursor, engine, `podium-cli`: Cursor takes allow rules only from a settings file shared with every Cursor session, which Podium does not edit
- cursor, engine, `podium-material`: unmeasured: whether Cursor asks before reading Podium's attachments outside the working folder; no signed-in Cursor account was available to the spike
- cursor, turn, `podium-cli`: Cursor takes allow rules only from a settings file shared with every Cursor session, which Podium does not edit
- cursor, turn, `podium-material`: unmeasured: whether Cursor asks before reading Podium's attachments outside the working folder; no signed-in Cursor account was available to the spike
- cursor, client, `workspace-trust`: Cursor keeps interactive folder trust in private state that Podium does not write
- cursor, client, `podium-cli`: Cursor takes allow rules only from a settings file shared with every Cursor session, which Podium does not edit
- cursor, client, `autonomy`: unmeasured: Cursor's mode flags were not run in its terminal UI (no signed-in Cursor account was available to the spike), so it starts in the mode its own settings choose
- cursor, client, `quiet-start`: unmeasured: no signed-in Cursor account was available to the spike
- cursor, client, `podium-material`: unmeasured: whether Cursor asks before reading Podium's attachments outside the working folder; no signed-in Cursor account was available to the spike
- antigravity, terminal, `workspace-trust`: Antigravity owns its initial workspace trust confirmation; approve it in the native terminal
- antigravity, turn, `autonomy`: Antigravity print mode cannot forward interactive permission questions; use its terminal for supervised work
- antigravity, client, `workspace-trust`: Antigravity owns its initial workspace trust confirmation; approve it in the native terminal
